newsitem.title: GERMANY: Turkish president visits Kohl amid Kurd protests.
newsitem.headline: Turkish president visits Kohl amid Kurd protests.

text.p: Turkish President Suleyman Demirel met German Chancellor Helmut Kohl on Tuesday while around 200 people demonstrated against Turkey's human rights policies outside the chancellery.

Demirel, whose four-day state visit to Germany began on Monday, had already run into several hundred protestors in Berlin who were protesting against alleged human rights violations against separatist Kurds in Turkey.

Protected by a tight security cordon, Demirel visited Kohl at noon before setting off for further meetings with other German political leaders including the parliamentary leader of the opposition Social Democrats Rudolf Scharping.
He was also scheduled to meet Joschka Fischer, the parliamentary leader of the Greens.
Several Kurdish groups have spoken out against his visit.

"Demirel's policies stand for the suppression of the Kurdish people," said Mehmet Tanriverdi, chairman of the Kurdish community in Germany. "The German government should immediately break off its economic and military support for Turkey."

The association of Kurdish groups (KOMKAR) said in a statement Demirel has held high offices in Turkey for 30 years and was "primarily responsible for the permanent and systematic human rights violations in Turkey".

In Berlin on Monday evening a group of about 150 demonstrators, led by Amnesty International, booed and whistled as Demirel entered the city hall. Police struggled with a number of demonstrators and several were detained.
Security was tight because of police concerns there might be disturbances from the outlawed Kurdish Workers Party (PKK). Police and the PKK have clashed several times in recent years.
